payload.answer: The CAP theorem states that in a distributed system, you can guarantee at most two out of three properties: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance [1]. Consistency means every read receives the most recent write, while Availability ensures every request gets a response regardless of network issues [1]. Partition Tolerance requires the system to keep operating despite network failures, which is mandatory in real-world distributed systems [1]. Because partitions are inevitable, architects must choose between prioritizing consistency or availability based on their specific needs [2].
